findings.evidence: The definition at lines 126–128 is `transpose (i.out * D.out) = D.outᵀ * i.outᵀ`; transposing `Γ₁ D.out Γ₂` reverses the subgroups to `Γ₂ᵀ D.outᵀ Γ₁ᵀ`. Lines 20–27 themselves show representative changes act through `hᵀ`, while `Gamma1Image` is defined at `HeckeRing/GL2/Gamma1.lean:67` from Γ₁(N), whose transpose exchanges its lower-left and upper-right congruence conditions.
findings.fix: Reformulate the generalized operator with the correctly transposed source/target subgroups (and prove the required relationships), or restrict the API to triples with explicit transpose-stability hypotheses. Do not present this instantiation as an operator on Γ₁(N)-invariant forms until that orientation mismatch is resolved.
findings.issue: `(σᵢδ)ᵀ` represents right cosets of the transposed double coset `Γ₂ᵀδᵀΓ₁ᵀ`, not right cosets `Γ₁(σᵢδ)ᵀ`; consequently Γ₁-invariance does not justify the claims at lines 25–27 and 161–168. This was harmless for transpose-stable `SLnZ 2`, but `Gamma1Image N` is not transpose-stable.

summary: The arbitrary-triple generalization retains a transpose argument that is valid for transpose-stable `SL₂(ℤ)` but not for the motivating `Γ₁(N)` triple, so it does not represent the claimed double-coset action.
